name: Inez Park
life: “I still remember trading days off with a colleague before we became friends.” On Monday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Inez checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I took everyone's unwanted Saturdays last year. I kept the tally because asking directly felt too much like begging.
appearance: Inez has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, and a favorite piece of clothing, a red windbreaker. It usually goes with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. When somebody else has the floor, Inez presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Inez talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Inez's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To ask for one of the Saturdays already earned.
family: Vera Baines is Inez’s stepsibling. Inez offers the first invitation. Vera gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The missing Sunday*, Vera says, “I have the Sunday key and normally clean silently.”
connections: Nia Brooks. A funeral slot is covered using one of the unwanted Saturdays still on the informal tally.
